## PRIMARY INFECTION (CHICKENPOX)
## ________________________________
## Immunocompetent patients
## ________________________________
## Prevention
Vaccinate all adults without evidence of immunity except for pregnant women.
Test antibody first in adults who have uncertain history of chickenpox or
vaccination.
Give Varicella vaccine x 2, 2nd dose 4-8 weeks after 1st dose
## Treatment
Therapy must be started within 24 hrs onset of rash.
Acyclovir 800 mg PO 5x/d for 5-7 days ($) [R]
## Alternative
Therapy must be started within 24 hrs onset of rash.
Valacyclovir 1 gm PO q8h for 5 days ($) [R]
## ________________________________
## Immunocompromised patients
## ________________________________
## Prevention
Immunocompromised patients without prior immunity to varicella who are at risk
for disease include: patients with malignancy, current immunosuppressive
therapy, or HIV infection. Vaccination is not recommended while patients are
immunocompromised.
Contact Infectious Diseases for more information.
## Treatment for mild to moderate disease
Acyclovir 800 mg PO 5x/day for 7 days ($) [R]
< OR >
Valacyclovir 1000 mg PO q8h for 7 days ($) [R]
## Treatment for severe disease, or if mild to moderate disease doesn't improve on
## above therapy
Acyclovir 10 mg/kg IV q8h for 7 days ($$) [R]
References:
Kim et al. Annals Intern Med. 2018, 168(3):210-220
Sanford keyword: Varicella-Zoster Virus
Mandell chapter: Chickenpox and Herpes Zoster (Varicella-Zoster Virus)
